Binary 'any exposure' = visited at least one such domain in the ~4-week period.

title: Exposure to low-credibility online health content is limited and is concentrated among older adults

quote:
comparing retailers’ recommendations with product datasheets, we found that 88.2% of
recommendations standards were incorrectly followed with the result that dosing was
either excessive or insufficient and accurate less than 12% of time.
date: not stated in the text (article received 14 June 2021)
moderator_quote:
Then, converted dosages were classified as correct if they fell within the lower and upper
bounds from datasheets, as overuse if higher than the upper bound, and as underuse if lower
than the lower bound.
ground_truth_detail: Researchers harmonised retailer-named pests and commercial products with OpenRefine, matched them to national pesticide databases and to a locally built pest synonymy table, then compared the recommendation against the manufacturer's product datasheet in a four-step procedure (pest identification, pest-product type match, crop-pest presence on the datasheet, dose within datasheet bounds). Dose conversions from local units used an expert-built conversion table. No inter-coder reliability statistic reported; the ground truth is documentary (datasheets), not a rater panel.

title: Uptake of the COVID-19 vaccine and its association with vaccine information and misinformation in Malawi

denominator: 895 Malawian adults aged 18+ attending outpatient, non-communicable disease or HIV clinics at 32 health facilities, recruited by systematic random sampling (every second person in the queue); AAPOR RR3 response rate 95.1%
definition: The paper does not define misinformation formally; it operationalizes it as "ten common statements (circulating conspiracy theories in Malawi) about COVID-19 and the COVID-19 vaccine", and states "exposure to misinformation, measured here by familiarity with conspiracy theories".
quote: Respondents reported having heard a median of 5 of the 10 surveyed conspiracy theories. The most commonly heard were “The spread of COVID-19 is a deliberate attempt to reduce the size of the global population” (80.7% of respondents [SE 16.2]) and “The COVID-19 virus is a hoax” (74.1% of respondents) [SE 15.7] (Fig. 3, Supplementary Data 2).

ground_truth_detail: Respondent self-report of having heard each pre-specified statement; the statements were pre-classified by the authors as conspiracy theories drawn from prior documentation of circulating claims in Malawi (refs 30, 31). title: Mapping the Infodemic: Geolocating Reddit Users and Unsupervised Topic Modeling of COVID-19-Related Misinformation
value_raw: 5014 labeled Reddit data comments, with 3439 labeled as true and 1575 as false (1575/5014 = 31.4%)

denominator: 5,014 manually labelled COVID-19 vaccine-related Reddit comments, drawn from 5,853 comments by users geolocated to U.S. cities/counties, themselves filtered from ~17.7 million keyword-collected Reddit comments
definition: The World Health Organization (WHO) called this an "infodemic," which means that there is too much information, some of which is true and some of which is not, which makes it hard for people to find reliable sources and advice
quote: After filtering, we assembled a final dataset of 5014 labeled Reddit data comments, with 3439 labeled as true and 1575 as false.

ground_truth_detail: Four researchers manually labelled each comment true or false on the basis of context, mood and overall message; no codebook, external fact-check source or guideline standard is described; inter-annotator agreement Cohen's kappa = 0.82

title: Presentation of benefits and harms of antidepressants on websites: A cross-sectional study
measure_type: % of websites attributing depression to a chemical imbalance or claiming antidepressants fix that imbalance (a claim with no scientific support)
denominator: 39 popular depression/antidepressant websites from 10 English- or Nordic-language countries, selected from the top of Google searches
definition: Information that 'conflicted with the scientific evidence'; the conclusion calls it 'The widespread misinformation'; assessed 'whether the information presented was trustworthy, given the available evidence'
quote: Twenty-nine (74%) websites attributed depression to a “chemical imbalance” or claimed they could ﬁx or correct that imbalance. Examples of misleading claims are shown in Table 5.
moderator_quote: We tried to mimic what most people would do when searching for information on the Internet and therefore chose easily accessible websites, which appeared at the top of a Google search. We searched the term depression and when this did not provide information about pharmacological therapy, we searched the terms antidepressants or depression therapy.
ground_truth_detail: Two authors extracted data (one on English-language sites, one on Nordic-language sites), doubts resolved by discussion; websites assessed against a list of 14 predefined criteria referenced to meta-analyses, systematic reviews, Cochrane reviews and FDA/TGA warnings. moderator_quote: Based on a list of 14 predeﬁned criteria, we assessed whether the information presented was trustworthy, given the available evidence (see Table 3).
ground_truth_detail: Two authors extracted data, doubts resolved by discussion; judged against predefined criteria 8-9, referenced to a benzodiazepine-SSRI dependence comparison and systematic reviews of withdrawal symptoms. No inter-rater reliability statistic reported.

title: Why do people share ideologically extreme, false, and misleading content on social media? A self-report and trace data-based analysis of countermedia content dissemination on facebook and twitter
value_raw: 196/678 non-zero countermedia sharers; "The majority of respondents (71.1%) did not share any countermedia items."
measure_type: % of panellists whose Facebook posting history contained at least one countermedia (fake-news domain) link
denominator: 678 US adult Facebook users in the Facebook analytic sample (Qualtrics panel, active on both Facebook and Twitter, complete self-report data)
definition: countermedia content, or web-based, ideologically extreme information that uses false, biased, misleading, and hyper-partisan claims to counter the knowledge produced by the mainstream news media
quote: In the Facebook sample, a total of 1,152 countermedia content shares were identified. The maximum number of pieces of content shared by a single user was 171. The majority of respondents (71.1%) did not share any countermedia items. [...] In the case of Facebook, we observed a comparatively greater number of cases with non-zero share counts for both the countermedia (n = 196) and mainstream news (n = 512) variables.
date: posts from 1 August 2015 to 6 June 2017; survey and data harvest 7 March 2017 to 6 June 2017
moderator_quote: To create the final sharing measure, we summed the number of posts containing countermedia links for each user. [...] In total, we identified 106 countermedia websites.
ground_truth_detail: Domain list built by pooling published fake-news domain lists from About.com, Aloisius, CBS News, The Daily Dot, Fake News Watch, Fake News Checker, Melissa Zimdars, NPR, Snopes Field Guide, The New Republic and U.S. News and World Report; a site had to appear on at least two lists, was manually reviewed to be predominantly political/social and not parody, giving 106 countermedia websites (62 of which were actually shared). No inter-coder reliability reported; the authors themselves note the lists are criticised for containing hyper-partisan rather than outright false sites (note 7).

title: Why do people share ideologically extreme, false, and misleading content on social media? A self-report and trace data-based analysis of countermedia content dissemination on facebook and twitter

A large majority (95.0%) of respondents did not share any countermedia content. [...] In the case of Twitter, the exceptionally small number of cases with non-zero countermedia sharing counts (n = 27) resulted in concerns related to power
date: posts from 1 August 2015 to 6 June 2017; survey and data harvest 7 March 2017 to 6 June 2017
moderator_quote: A Python script was used to extract all social media posts that contained articles from the countermedia identified domains. Content from a total of 62 domains was shared across both platforms
ground_truth_detail: Same 106-domain pooled fake-news list as the Facebook row; site had to appear on at least two of eleven published lists and be manually confirmed political/social and non-parody. No inter-coder reliability reported.

title: Media framing of spiders may exacerbate arachnophobic sentiments
value_raw: 73% of media reports (of n = 314); abstract and discussion state 70% / 'Over 70%'
measure_type: % of spider-related news articles containing one or more factual errors
denominator: 314 spider-related media reports published in Italian online newspapers 2010-2020 and referring to human-spider encounters in Italy
definition: 'Providing the photo of a wrong species, calling a spider 'insect' or stating that a spider 'stings' rather than 'bites', are small errors that contribute to spread misinformation'
quote: One or more error types were present in 73% of media reports (Figure 3).
date: media reports published between 2010 and 2020 (2020 covered only up to February); Facebook share data extracted 2 March 2020
moderator_quote: We carried out online searches in Italian with Google news, choosing multiple keyword combinations. ... This search strategy led to a total of 260 searches: 2 actions ('morso' or 'puntura') × 13 species names (the general words 'ragno', 4 Latin, and 8 vernacular species names) × 10 years (2010-2020). For each unique keyword search, we checked news up to the final available page in Google news, collecting all the media reports referring to one or more encounters in Italy between humans and spiders.
ground_truth_detail: Coding by the authors, who are practising arachnologists acting as consultants to Italian anti-poison centres; errors checked against scientific literature on Italian spiders (Pantini & Isaia 2019) and taxonomic/medical sources. No inter-coder reliability statistic reported for the error coding (sensationalism was scored independently by three authors and resolved by consensus).

title: Leveraging Social Media as a Thermometer to Gauge Patient and Caregiver Concerns: COVID-19 and Prostate Cancer

quote: Misinformation was present in 7% of COVID-19–related posts.
moderator_quote: Manual qualitative analysis was performed for all posts to the Inspire Us TOO Prostate Cancer online support and discussion community and Reddit that mentioned COVID, COVID-19, or coronavirus. Posts were coded independently by four trained coders using a codebook created and refined by the study team.
ground_truth_detail: Posts coded independently by four trained coders using a codebook created and refined by the study team; the codebook covered contributor characteristics, prostate cancer characteristics, post topic and presence of misinformation. No inter-coder reliability statistic and no adjudication procedure reported, and no external ground-truth source (fact-checks, guidelines) named.

Questionnaire reviewed in advance by three social science research professionals and piloted; fieldwork by Netquest (ISO 26362 certified, invitation-only panel).

Of the analyzed videos, 87.72% (100/114) provided use-
ful and 12.28% (14/114) contained misleading information.
moderator_quote: The videos meeting the inclusion criteria were evaluated in terms of usefulness and categorized as useful and misleading. ground_truth_detail: Two rheumatologists (M.E.O. and O.Z.) analysed all 114 videos blindly; discrepancies resolved by reassessment and consensus. Inter-observer agreement Cohen's kappa 0.925 [95% CI 0.883-1.000]. Ground truth is the coders' judgment of scientific accuracy, referenced in the discussion to ACR and EULAR guidelines rather than to a formal fact-check list.

title: Qualitative Evaluation of YouTube Videos on Dental Fear, Anxiety and Phobia
measure_type: % of analysed dental fear/anxiety/phobia YouTube videos containing misleading information
denominator: 145 English-language YouTube videos on dental fear, dental anxiety or dental phobia, drawn from the 100 most-viewed results for each of three search terms (300 screened, 181 after duplicate removal, 145 eligible)
definition: No formal definition given; items are labelled 'misleading information' / 'Misinformation' and each is paired with a corrective statement beginning 'Truth:'.
quote: 17 videos (11.7%) contained misleading information. The Cohen’s kappa of whether the included videos contained misleading information was 93%.

title: The Assessment of TikTok as a Source of Quality Health Information on Varicoceles

moderator_quote: Using the key word “varicocele,” the ﬁrst 225 videos delivered by TikTok’s “top” sorting process on May 24, 2022 were retrieved. This sorting is based on the highest TikTok user engagement.

denominator: 562 YouTube videos containing COVID-19 medical or epidemiological information, from the first 50 relevant results (75 for English) for “coronavirus” and “COVID-19” plus a language specifier, in 11 languages
definition: “misleading (scientifically inaccurate information or content that is not evidence‐based)”
quote: The majority of videos were classified as informative (471/562, 83.8%) with over 229 million views, while misleading videos constituted 12/562 (2.13%) of total videos, with a total number of views at over 75,000.
moderator_quote: The first 50 relevant results were screened, and relevant videos that contained COVID‐19 medical or epidemiological information were included. ... After the initial 50 videos were screened, this process was repeated with the second and third search terms for a total of 50 videos for each language (with the exception of English for which 75 videos were included due to the higher volume of videos available).
ground_truth_detail: Two independent raters per language, each with a medical background and proficient in that language; coding criteria for the MICI components developed from WHO and CDC guidelines; Cohen's kappa per language ranged 0.44 (French) to 1.00 (Nigerian Pidgin, Twi, Amharic), all p < 0.001

Of the 1200 tweets, the final coding data set contained 504 (42% random sample) tweets.

ground_truth_detail: Unsupervised topic models (biterm topic model on D1 to pick the most polemical topic; LDA-U with 30 topics on author-aggregated tweets in D3), with topics labelled by the single author using coherence scores and an ad hoc Italian reference corpus of three books; no human item-level coding and no reliability statistics

title: Fact-checking of political information about the Russo-Ukrainian conflict
value_raw: 54.7% of 128 fact-checking reports rated invalid (False 32.0% + Miscaptioned 21.1% + Outdated 1.6%)
measure_type: % of fact-checked claims about the Russo-Ukrainian conflict rated invalid (False, Miscaptioned or Outdated)
denominator: 128 Snopes fact-checking reports on the Russo-Ukrainian conflict published 24 February 2022 - 28 June 2023, retrieved with the search terms 'Russia AND Ukraine' and 'Ukraine AND war'
definition: "fact-checking can be defined as 'the practice of systematically publishing assessments of the validity of claims made by public officials and institutions with an explicit attempt to identify whether a claim is factual'"; ratings: valid (True, Correct Attribution), invalid (False, Miscaptioned, Outdated), mixed
quote: The share of negatively coloured assessments (False, Miscaptioned, and Outdated) indicative of the invalidity of the claims was 54.7%, while the share of positive ratings (True, Correct Attribution) was 26.7%. The share of mixed assessments was 15.6%.
moderator_quote: The empirical data include altogether 128 fact-checking reports (for short, fact-checks) dealing with the Russo-Ukrainian conflict. The reports were published within the period of 24 February 2022-28 June 2023. The reports were identified from the website of Snopes.com using the search terms Russia AND Ukraine, and Ukraine AND war. All of the 128 fact-checks dealing with the above topic were downloaded for closer analysis.
ground_truth_detail: Ratings assigned by professional Snopes.com fact-checkers using Snopes' own 20-category rating scheme (9 categories occurred in the sample); the study author regrouped these into valid / invalid / mixed. Single coder (the author) for the regrouping and for the evaluation-ground coding; no inter-rater reliability reported.

title: Fact-checking of political information about the Russo-Ukrainian conflict
measure_type: % of fact-checked claims about the Russo-Ukrainian conflict rated 'False' (demonstrably false) by Snopes
denominator: 128 Snopes fact-checking reports on the Russo-Ukrainian conflict published 24 February 2022 - 28 June 2023
definition: "False. The primary elements of a claim are demonstrably false."
quote: False 32.0 True 21.9 Miscaptioned 21.1
moderator_quote: The subgroup of valid include two ratings: True and Correct Attribution, while claims rated as False, Miscaptioned, and Outdated formed the subgroup labelled as invalid.
ground_truth_detail: Rating assigned by professional Snopes.com fact-checkers under their published rating definitions; no inter-rater reliability reported by the study.

title: Long-term assessment of social amplification of risk during COVID-19: challenges to public health agencies amid misinformation and vaccine stance
measure_type: % of Finnish-language COVID-19 vaccination-related tweets classified as containing misinformation
denominator: 1,683,700 vaccination/COVID-19-related tweets in Finnish collected from Twitter with 147 query keywords (724,214 retweets, 57,865 quotes, 901,621 original tweets), from 60,560 unique accounts
definition: "misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information that is intentionally or unintentionally disseminated"
quote: 460,087 tweets (27.3%) as containing misinformation. (See Table 1 and Table 2 in the Online Appendix for more details.)
moderator_quote: The dataset comprises 1,683,700 tweets from 60,560 unique Twitter accounts
ground_truth_detail: FinBERT (Turku University Finnish BERT) fine-tuned on 4,150 randomly sampled tweets manually annotated by four Finnish-speaking research assistants after six rounds of training, using the Memon and Carley misinformation codebook; Krippendorff's alpha 0.668 for misinformation (0.693 for vaccine stance). No classifier precision/recall reported.

title: Characterisation of social media conversations on syphilis: An unobtrusive observational study
value_raw: 240 of 1762 tweets (14%) deemed medically incorrect; 1484 (84%) medically correct; 38 (2%) accuracy could not be determined
measure_type: % of syphilis tweets categorised as a medical resource that were judged medically incorrect
denominator: 1,762 tweets categorised as a medical resource, from a systematic 10% sample (n = 11,113) of the 111,388 English-language tweets containing the word 'syphilis' posted on Twitter in 2019
definition: The paper uses no formal definition of misinformation; accuracy is operationalised as whether a medical-resource tweet is 'medically correct or incorrect', with the discussion framing incorrect content as 'Health misinformation' and 'Incorrect medical information'
quote: Of 1762 tweets (16%) categorised as a medical resource, 1484 (84%) were medically correct and 240 (14%) were medically incorrect; for 38 (2%), medical accuracy could not be judged from the information posted.
date: 1 January - 31 December 2019 (dataset extracted 8 September 2020 via TrackMyHashtag)
moderator_quote: All tweets assigned to the category of medical resource were reviewed by an infectious disease registrar (AF) to determine whether they were medically correct or incorrect. The content of the text, any associated still images or videos and links provided within each tweet were considered in the assessment.
ground_truth_detail: Content categories assigned by one researcher (AD) in a two-round pass using a 10-category scheme adapted from Chew et al. (2010), opening the tweet online and reading it in thread context where needed; clinical accuracy of every medical-resource tweet then judged by an infectious disease registrar (AF), considering tweet text, images, videos and links. No inter-rater reliability statistic is reported and each coding stage had a single coder.

title: Dueling COVID-19 misinformation: Perceptions and behavior of the rural population from South Asian countries
value_raw: 92.98% of the participants perceived the presence of COVID-19 misinformation to varying degrees around them (N = 399)
measure_type: % of survey respondents who perceived the presence of COVID-19 misinformation around them to any degree
denominator: 399 rural adult respondents from Bangladesh (n = 49), India (n = 300) and Pakistan (n = 50), convenience sample
definition: "information that is false but not created with the intention of causing harm"; fake news = "false stories that appear to be news, spread on the internet or using other media" (UNESCO, 2018); the study is limited to "misinformation" and "fake news", with fake news and made-up news used interchangeably
quote: Results indicate that 92.98% of the participants perceived the presence of COVID-19 misinformation to varying degrees around them with less than 10% finding it easy to verify the accuracy of the information.
date: April-July 2022 (Bangladesh and Pakistan May-June 2022; India April-June 2022)
moderator_quote: The study included a total of 399 participants from rural regions of three SA countries: Bangladesh, India, and Pakistan.
ground_truth_detail: Self-reported perception on a 5-point scale (a great deal = 5 ... not at all = 1); questionnaire adapted from a Pew Research Center (2021) survey, translated into Bengali, Hindi and Urdu; responses recorded by trained data collectors reading questions aloud. No inter-coder reliability applicable.

title: Accuracy, readability, and quality of websites about metastatic renal cell carcinoma treatment
value_raw: Twelve (31%) websites contained at least 1 incorrect statement; 12/39
measure_type: % of patient-facing websites containing at least one statement incorrect against clinical guidelines
denominator: 39 eligible English-language patient-facing websites about metastatic renal cell carcinoma treatment, screened from the first 25 links of 36 keyword permutations across 3 search engines (2,700 queries)
definition: "Correctness by identifying incorrect statements that were inconsistent with guidelines"; the paper frames these as "outdated, misleading, or grossly false information" and refers to "harm from misinformation"
quote: Twelve (31%) websites had ≥1 incorrect statement, such as listing homeopathy or hormone therapy as mRCC treatment options, or including outdated statements.
moderator_quote: Across 3 Internet search engines, 25 links of 36 permutations of mRCC keywords and their synonyms were screened for eligibility.
ground_truth_detail: One medical oncologist (DHK) reviewed all websites and flagged statements inconsistent with the NCCN Kidney Cancer Version 4.2023 guidelines; statements that were not clearly incorrect were discussed with a second medical oncologist (AD or KF). No inter-rater reliability statistic is reported for the correctness domain (the reported Cronbach's alphas of 0.996 and 0.846 apply to the completeness checklist and to DISCERN respectively).

measure_type: % of TikTok #mentalhealth videos giving advice or information that clinical experts coded as misleading

definition: Some misleading videos contained overtly inaccurate facts; others lacked sufficient context to make conclusions and risked leading to inappropriate conclusions or self-diagnoses.
quote: advice given was coded as non-misleading in 67.0% ( n = 215) of videos and misleading in 33.0% ( n = 106).
moderator_quote: A second coding team of clinical experts, consisting of a licensed clinical psychologist (JS) and two psychiatrists (SM, RS) were involved in assessing the quality and accuracy of videos giving advice and information ( n  = 319).
ground_truth_detail: A second coding team of clinical experts (licensed clinical psychologist JS, psychiatrists SM and RS) viewed each of the 319 advice videos and labelled it misleading, non-misleading, or unable to determine; true disagreements occurred for 23.1% (n = 74) and 'unable to determine' clashes for 26.5% (n = 85), resolved by a third coder; 72.3% agreement reported. title: Sourcing and Automation of Political News and Information over Social Media in the United States, 2016-2018
measure_type: share of all divisive and conspiracy source shares that came from high-volume amplifier accounts (0.11% of users)
denominator: conc_group_pct denominator: 3.69m Twitter users in the 2016 election hashtag sample (Table 1). conc_share_pct denominator: all tweets sharing Divisive and Conspiracy Sources in that sample (674,269 per Table 2).
definition: "We developed the concept of 'junk news,' which refers to sources that deliberately publish misleading, deceptive, or incorrect information packaged as real news."
quote: For Polarizing and Conspiracy Content, the number of total shares almost doubled to 180,337 shares generating 27.8 percent of all tweets in this category.
moderator_quote: We identified amplifier accounts as those that posted 50 times a day or more using one of the selected hashtags during the data collection period.
ground_truth_detail: Amplifier status assigned by a volume threshold (50+ tweets/day on the study hashtags), not by a bot classifier; the authors note the threshold was set because 'we have identified very few human users that tweeted more than 49.5 times on average per day' and that 'more complex methods using machine learning yield comparative numbers of positives'. The content side uses the same 710-domain hand-coded typology (Krippendorff's alpha = 0.89).

title: Research note: The spread of political misinformation on online subcultural platforms

denominator: 182 hostnames shared on 4chan /pol/ with more than 400 mentions over the period, hand-coded by the research team
definition: propaganda: "websites that misrepresent facts for political ends"

moderator_quote: We searched TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts for epilepsy short-form videos using the free text term “epilepsy.” We chose such a broad, English search term to capture the widest and most international range of videos concerning epilepsy. For this search, we used a new, blank account. ... A total of 750 video URLs were recorded, 250 from each social media platform ... This URL recording phase was conducted on June 8th, 2025 | Videos were classified as containing disinformation/misinformation if they contained information in contradiction to clinical recommendations.
ground_truth_detail: Three evaluators (a student living with epilepsy, an adult-neurology resident, and an epileptologist) independently watched every video and recorded yes/no for disinformation/misinformation on a standardised form; if the senior evaluator plus one other agreed, that verdict stood; if the two junior evaluators agreed against the senior, all three met to rewatch and decide. Interrater agreement 83.5% (95% CI: 80.6-86.0).

definition: Operationalised as visits to 'untrustworthy websites', a list of 1,796 domains for the 2020 US election context combining Guess, Nyhan and Reifler (2020) (itself 490 domains from Grinberg et al. 2019 plus 66 from Allcott and Gentzkow 2017) with 1,240 domains NewsGuard classified as 'repeatedly publishing false content' during the 2020 study period.

moderator_quote: To identify participant visits to untrustworthy websites, we followed the procedure used in recent studies (Moore, Dahlke, and Hancock 2023; W. Ahmad et al. 2024) by creating a comprehensive list of 1,796 domains for the 2020 US election context. ... Our primary independent variable, binary untrustworthy website exposure, was coded “1” if a participant visited at least one unique domain from this list during the Wave 2 observation period (September 19, 2020, to December 7, 2020), and “0” otherwise. Any recorded page view to a URL within a listed domain constituted a visit.
ground_truth_detail: A 1,796-domain untrustworthy-website list assembled by the authors: the Guess, Nyhan and Reifler (2020) list (490 Grinberg et al. 2019 domains + 66 Allcott and Gentzkow 2017 domains) plus 1,240 domains rated by NewsGuard, an organisation of journalists rating news sources, as 'repeatedly publishing false content' during the 2020 study period. No item-level verification; no coder reliability applies because no human coding of content was done.

value_raw: 138/150 containing incorrect/incomplete frequency (92%); 12/150 containing the promised frequency (8%)
measure_type: % of healing-frequency audio items whose audio did not contain the Hz value promised in the item's title, by FFT spectrum analysis
denominator: 150 digital music items ACROSS SEVEN PLATFORMS THAT ALREADY MAKE A HEALING-FREQUENCY CLAIM: every item in the sample was selected because it named a specific Hz value (432, 528 or 639 Hz) in its title or description and had at least 10,000 interactions. The denominator is therefore topic-conditional and popularity-truncated, not all music content or all health content on these platforms.
definition: The paper speaks of 'digital disinformation' and 'the gap between the perception of miraculous frequencies created by popular culture and neuroscientific reality'; it gives no formal definition of misinformation and operationalises accuracy purely as technical frequency correspondence.
quote: Table 2. Distribution of the technical accuracy of the contents | Technical Criterion | Number of Contents (n=150) | % | Containing the Promised Frequency | 12 | %8 | Containing Incorrect/Incomplete Frequency | 138 | %92 ... The fact that the promised Hertz value was found in only 12 contents (8%) points to a serious inconsistency regarding the technical accuracy of content marketed as healing frequencies.
date: not stated; article received 11 December 2025, accepted 10 April 2026
moderator_quote: A total of 150 different digital contents were selected using the criterion sampling technique, one of the purposive sampling methods. The main criteria were that the content had received at least 10,000 interactions and included a specific Hz value in its title or description section, such as 432 Hz, 528 Hz, or 639 Hz.
ground_truth_detail: Instrumental verification, not human judgement: each file analysed three times with a digital spectrum analyser and Voxengo SPAN at 44.1 kHz, dominant frequency compared with the titled value at +/-3 Hz tolerance. Two independent researchers coded the data set and Krippendorff alpha was 0.82, but that alpha covers the discursive/thematic coding, not the FFT test, which is instrumental and needs no rater agreement.

measure_type: % of observed community-health-worker home-visit interactions in which at least one health-misinformation claim was raised
denominator: 480 OBSERVED FACE-TO-FACE CHW-COMMUNITY MEMBER INTERACTIONS, recorded during routine home visits by 36 CHWs across eight purposively selected community health centres in four provinces over six months. The denominator is a count of observed conversations, NOT posts, NOT items of media content and NOT people: the same community member could in principle appear in more than one interaction, and the paper does not say how many distinct households or individuals the 480 interactions cover.
definition: No formal definition is given; the paper works with 'vernacular health misinformation', false health claims moving through oral networks, citing Wardle and Derakhshan's information-disorder framework
quote: Of the 480 observed interactions, 198 (41.3%) contained at least one misinformation encounter.
moderator_quote: Structured observations covered 480 CHW-community member interactions, recorded during routine home visits over six months (February to July 2024). Each observation was documented using a standardised field note template capturing the health topic discussed, presence and type of misinformation, the CHW's response strategy, and the community member's reaction.
ground_truth_detail: Two field researchers coded all observations against a deductive coding framework; inter-rater agreement 84.6 per cent, Cohen's kappa = 0.79. No detail on how disagreements were resolved, no codebook reproduced, no per-domain reliability.
